messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: SLO breach detected on /v1/stream endpoint. p99 latency > 4s for last 10m, p95 elevated. Autoscale healthy, error rates unchanged. Alerting oncall.

pagerduty: Paging oncall -> @sre-oncall (high) :bell:

sre-oncall: on it. looking at traces and streaming telemetry now. anyone seeing customer tickets? @cs-ops

cs-ops: saw two CS tickets about slow streaming for an internal customer (acct: greenwave). Marked P3 but escalating given SLOs.

anya: I see a spike in long-tail tokens (requests with > 1024 tokens). p99 jumps coincide with a calibration job finish ~03:12 UTC. Running a quick diff on precision profiles.

matt: calibration job? which one? last deploy was a config push for quant profiles yesterday.

leo: confirm: calib job calib-2026-03-14-int8 finished at 03:11:43. It adjusted per-layer quant scales to reduce MSE. Rolling out across serving-pool-a.

sre-oncall: timeline lines up. Querying model runtime logs for dequant / kv cache stalls.

sre-oncall: logs show repeated dequant memcpy waits on GPU for some streams: 50–120ms stalls per step for long sequences. Stack points to int8 dequant path in kernel dequantize_fp8_to_fp16 (approx).

anya: interesting — the kernel path was added to speed up token generation at short sequences but might mis-handle long KV interactions. Could be a regression for streaming where KV reads are hot.

matt: can we route traffic to the float (fp16) model variant while we investigate? We have variant tag model:open-600m-fp16 available in the routing pool.

sre-oncall: yes. I'll create a temporary policy to route 100% of streaming calls from prod to fp16 for the impacted model family. Doing a canary first across 10%.

deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-policy/update -> canary 10% -> modelset: open-600m-fp16. CI checks passed.

leo: dashboards: after canary kick, p99 for canary dropped back to baseline. Non-canary still high.

sre-oncall: increasing to 100% routing to fp16 now. Policy applied: all streaming -> fp16 fallback. Monitoring.

matt: granular ask: capture a few traces with the int8 kernel enabled so ML team can reproduce locally. Can we preserve a couple of affected traces before rollback fully completes?

sre-oncall: yes, saving traces. Saved traces IDs: trace-6189, trace-6190, trace-6191. Linking to trace viewer: https://dash.redwood.internal/traces/trace-6189

anya: grabbing the traces. early look: KV dequant lock contention appears when sequence_length > 900 and batcher coalesces different step counts. Batcher coalescing + int8 dequant writebacks -> hotspot.

tara: from CS: two paying customers saw degraded UX (streaming stalls, occasional reconnects). Logging incidents with them. Customer impact window: 03:11–03:34 UTC. Estimated affected requests ~0.2% of total streaming requests.

cs-ops: onboarding note: greenwave wants a postmortem and ETA for permanent fix. Please record mitigation steps and timeline.

sre-oncall: mitigation summary posted to incident doc: rollback calib-2026-03-14-int8 -> completed at 03:21 UTC. All streaming traffic routed to fp16 until root cause fixed. Autoscaler kept capacity; no OOMs.

matt: next step: ML to bisect quant calibration change to identify layer(s) causing KV contention. Any hot layers in traces?

anya: preliminary: layers 8, 10 show much higher per-layer dequant throughput and lock acquisitions. Looks like a codepath where int8 dequant writes back into a shared staging buffer without per-stream indexing.

leo: creating an isolated perf test: reproduce with synthetic long-context workload (seq_len=1200) + batcher settings similar to prod: max_batch=64, batching_timeout=6ms.

sre-oncall: runbook pointer for routing fallback and rollback: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/quant/rollback

matt: to reduce customer impact while fix is developed, can we enable a hybrid policy: prefer fp16 for streams > 512 tokens and keep int8 for short ones? That would preserve cost benefits.

sre-oncall: yes we can do conditional routing based on sequence length header X-Seq-Len. I'll push policy: if X-Seq-Len > 512 -> fp16, else -> int8. Applying now.

deploy-bot: routing-policy/update applied: conditional seq_len threshold = 512

leo: early metrics: tail latency for streams >512 normalized to fp16 baseline, overall costs increased ~3% but p99 restored.

anya: ML note: we'll instrument per-layer atomic ops and add per-stream staging offsets in dequant kernel. Patch PR opened: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3928. Tests included.

matt: nice. estimate for patch + QA + canary on prod: ~8 hours. Can we keep hybrid routing until then? Also tag customer SLAs.

cs-ops: greenwave notified, they're okay with hybrid for now but requested ETA and follow-up. I'll keep them updated.

sre-oncall: monitoring: no further SLO breaches after policy change for last 15m. Will keep the incident open for postmortem.

anya: adding reproducer to ML repo and running GPU microbenchmarks. Will attach perf numbers to postmortem.

tara: filing incident in #postmortems with impact summary and timelines. I'll add customer communication draft.

matt: once PR lands, let's canary in serving-pool-a with reduced batcher coalescing to catch regressions early.

sre-oncall: ack. we'll schedule a 2-hour observation window post-canary.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: pr/3928 -> perf-canary. Notified @matt @anya @leo.

anya: thanks. ping me if you need binary rollback. I'll be oncall for ML changes today.

matt: great job triaging — :thumbsup:. Closing action items: 1) ML PR + perf data, 2) hybrid routing retained until fix, 3) CS follow-up, 4) postmortem.

sre-oncall: incident status: mitigated -> routing fallback + rollback applied. Keeping incident open for follow-up and postmortem duties. Will update when PR is canaried.

cs-ops: noted. will send final customer update after canary verification.

deploy-bot: automated note: incident channel archived metadata -> incident-2064123456."
